newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish cabinet clears new exports guarantee rules.
newsitem.headline: Polish cabinet clears new exports guarantee rules.

text.p: The Polish government on Tuesday approved new exports guarantee regulations aimed at stimulating sales to former Soviet Union countries, the acting foreign trade minister said.

"This project...will enable exporters who want to operate in higher-risk countries, mainly eastern markets, to have more confidence in planning their sales," Janusz Kaczurba told a news briefing. The scheme provides for creating a special fund supervised by the Credit Exports Insurance Corporation (KUKE) -- a government agency that has so far extended credit guarantees mainly for exports to Western countries.
The fund, which will back exports to high-risk countries, will be endowed with government-owned shares of several foreign trade companies and have a capital of 200 million zlotys, Kaczurba said.

Some of these shares now belong to the Polish Guarantee Fund (PFG) and the International Guarantee Corporation (MKK), two state-owned credit guarantees bodies that are due to be liquidated after bringing substantial losses.
Controversy over these losses were among the reasons for the dismissal of the previous foreign trade minister, Jacek Buchacz, earlier this year.
Several Polish banks, notably state-owned Bank Handlowy SA and Bank Rozwoju Eksportu SA, will have stakes in the new fund.
Under the new rules, KUKE, now supervised by the finance ministry, would be controlled by a committee comprising several economic ministers, who will devise credit guarantee policies.
